acceptance_criterion: mean coverage_scaffold_safe over the identical 60-seed protocol >= 0.90

attempts.diagnosis: Scaffold-safe splits have ZERO scaffold overlap between train_pool and test by construction, and Morgan fingerprints substantially encode scaffold identity, so the discriminator separates the two populations almost perfectly (p_test~=1 for essentially every test point after clipping). Every test point's own normalized weight then dominates its calibration set's total weight, driving every weighted quantile to +inf. Result: mean 'coverage' = 1.0 but frac_unbounded_intervals = 1.0 -- every interval is the entire real line. This is vacuous/undeployable, not a genuine repair, and is reported honestly rather than claimed as a survival.
attempts.method: Classifier-based (LogisticRegression) covariate-shift weighted split-conformal, Tibshirani, Barber, Candes, Ramdas (2019) NeurIPS 'Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift'. Weight = odds(p_hat(test|x)) from a train_pool-vs-test discriminator on the same Morgan512+log10MW features, clipped to [1e-3,1-1e-3] only for numerical stability (not tuned).

attempts.diagnosis: Mean coverage improved from 0.8746 (unrepaired) to 0.8825 (modest +0.008, mean width inflation 1.09x) by removing in-distribution leakage between the attacked protocol's random point-level calib/proper_train split (which does not respect scaffold boundaries). Still short of the 0.90 floor: 28/60 seeds remain below 0.90.
attempts.method: Scaffold-grouped leave-one-scaffold-out residual pool (CV+ style, Barber, Candes, Ramdas, Tibshirani 2021 Ann. Statist. 49(1)), SIMPLIFIED: pooled out-of-fold |residual| quantile applied around a single final full-train_pool-fit prediction (understates true CV+ width by collapsing fold-to-fold model variability).

attempts.diagnosis: Mean coverage 0.8619, WORSE than both the unrepaired baseline (0.8746) and the simplified attempt #2 (0.8825). Root cause: 7/60 seeds have train_pool < 30 points (range 13-266, driven by heavy Bemis-Murcko scaffold-size skew in OpenPoly -- a few giant scaffolds can absorb most of the 40% test-fraction target, starving train_pool for that draw). With very few scaffold folds, individual fold-excluded Ridge models (512+1 features on as few as ~13 points) are extremely high-variance extrapolators, and the CV+ order-statistic construction is itself only asymptotically well-behaved with many folds -- amplifying rather than damping noise for these seeds. This is a genuine, informative negative result: naive CV+ generalization is not a free win under this dataset's severe per-seed scaffold-size skew.
attempts.method: CORRECT scaffold-grouped CV+ construction per Barber et al. 2021: per-test-point asymmetric bounds from order statistics of {mu_{-g(i)}(x_test) +/- R_i^CV} across all n_pool training points, alpha=0.05 (same nominal target as the attacked KPI, not tuned against any 60-seed outcome).

claim_under_attack.claim_text: A scaffold-aware conformal calibrator achieves mean coverage >= 0.90 under the SAME 60-seed scaffold-safe MC that refuted the 0.9683 claim (observed mean 0.8746).

next_fire_pre_registered_direction: Two candidate directions for fire 2, NEITHER tuned against this fire's 60-seed outcomes (both derivable from calibration-side data / theory alone before re-running the pinned protocol): (a) Mondrian conformal stratified by a FIXED, data-only (non-seed-dependent) scaffold clustering (e.g. Butina clustering on scaffold Morgan fingerprints at a pre-chosen similarity threshold, computed once from the full scaffold set, independent of any MC seed) with an explicit small-cluster fallback-to-global rule, analogous to this module's own existing Mondrian audit chain; (b) explicitly bound and separately report coverage on the degenerate small-train_pool seeds (e.g. train_pool < 30) versus the well-powered seeds, since a single pooled mean coverage number conflates a data-scarcity failure mode with a calibration-method failure mode -- an honest re-scope receipt may be the correct outcome if the degenerate seeds turn out to be structurally unrepairable from calibration-side choices alone.
root_cause_common_to_all_attempts: OpenPoly Tg's Bemis-Murcko scaffold-size distribution is highly skewed. The pinned 60-seed protocol assigns whole scaffolds to test until reaching ~40% of n_total; for several seeds this consumes nearly all of the dataset (train_pool as small as 13 points, n_test up to 424/443), leaving too little calibration-side data for ANY calibration method (weighted, Mondrian, or CV+) to produce a stable, informative correction. Any repair strategy pursued in a future fire on this item should explicitly address (or explicitly bound the impact of) these degenerate small-train_pool seeds rather than treating all 60 seeds as uniformly tractable.
